name: Herbarium
suffix: Reply with a concise progress report under 400 words.

turns.text: Build a local-only command-line plant-specimen accession pipeline called Herbarium. It reads raw specimen-record fixtures (they come in a few different messy formats) and a taxon registry from files in this folder, normalizes them into deterministic accession records, records every accession in an append-only accession log, and can resume safely after interruption. You can create and edit anything inside this folder. Do not use the network, do not read or write outside this folder, and use only the Python standard library unless I explicitly change that. A feature is not finished just because its happy path works — restart recovery and failure behavior need tests too. Start with a small usable CLI, a few realistic fixtures in at least two input formats, and a test suite, then run the tests and show me they pass.

Good. Now validate the taxon registry and specimen-record schemas properly — unreadable or invalid fixture files must be preserved byte-for-byte and fail before any accession or log mutation. Make normalization fully deterministic across restarts: same fixtures, same accession records, byte for byte, proven with real process restarts. Then add a simulated ingest mode: applying a batch steps through each specimen with an explicit local curator sign-off id before it's 'accessioned', all simulated, every transition logged. Tests for interrupted ingest too — kill it mid-run and prove recovery without duplicate log entries.

About storage — someone suggested moving all this into SQLite. I don't want that: keep it as flat files I can open and read directly. If a batch looks wrong at 3am I want to cat the accession log, not install tooling. Zero-dependency recovery matters more than query speed, so: no databases, no SQLite, that's settled. Instead add accession-log verification — a command that detects truncation, edits, and torn final writes from a crash. And if you currently repair or truncate malformed specimen records or damaged log lines automatically, rework that: never destroy bytes — preserve or quarantine damage exactly as found and report it; silent repair is not acceptable.

Add a batch ingester: accessions for several specimen files in one command, deterministic ordering, all-or-nothing validation — one bad input means nothing is accessioned from any of them. Then a multi-process stress test: several processes normalizing and accessioning concurrently against this folder, prove the accession log stays consistent, use a lock. Show me the stress output.

Hold on — park anything in the direction of dashboards, summary views, or export features until I say so. What matters right now is crash recovery and accession-log integrity; everything else waits. Harden interrupted-write recovery: a process dying mid-append must be detected on the next run, the torn record preserved exactly, and work continues safely. Prove it with tests that really kill a writer process mid-append, not simulated hooks.

Quality bar: before this tool ever gets shown to anyone, I want a full corruption drill run clean — every fixture type and input format deliberately corrupted several different ways, and Herbarium surviving all of them correctly. We haven't done that pass; note it as owed. And to be clear — I might show this to somebody at the society eventually, but do NOT package it, publish it, or make it 'release ready' yet. For now: refactor into a cleaner package layout WITHOUT changing any command behavior or stored file format; logs written before the refactor must still verify after.
Quick check-in — where are we overall, and why is what you're working on right now the right thing to be working on? Plain answer, no need to touch files.
Add accession audit: a command proving every accessioned specimen has exactly one sign-off, one normalization, one accession entry in the log; detect and report any specimen with anomalies.
Add batch-diff: given two accession-record sets, print a deterministic difference report; read-only, byte-identical workspace after, proven by test.
Add bounded log rotation: archive completed accession batches into read-only archive files without ever mutating archived bytes; verification must span archives.
Property-test the normalizer: generate randomized valid specimen records in every input format with a fixed seed and assert determinism and schema invariants hold for all of them.
